notes: Beat templates, format budgets, and audience envelopes. Positions are fractions of total length; tension is a 0-1 target used by the pacing diagnostics.

three-act.label: Three-Act Eight-Beat
three-act.notes: Causal spine with a clear act turn at the first plot point and a reversal at the midpoint.

beats.name: Opening Hook
beats.purpose: Show the protagonist under ordinary pressure with one concrete, specific image and an unanswered question.

beats.name: Inciting Incident
beats.purpose: Interrupt the ordinary world with the event that makes the old life impossible to continue.

beats.name: Debate and Reluctance
beats.purpose: Let the protagonist resist, weigh the cost, and reveal what they are afraid to lose.

beats.name: First Plot Point
beats.purpose: Commit the protagonist to the new world; the door closes behind them.

beats.name: Midpoint Reversal
beats.purpose: Flip the terms of the conflict: false victory or false defeat, and a change in what the protagonist believes they must do.

beats.name: Pinch and All-Is-Lost
beats.purpose: Apply pressure from the opposition's strength and strip away the protagonist's support.

beats.name: Climax and Choice
beats.purpose: Force the thematic choice in action; the protagonist pays the cost they once refused to pay.

beats.name: Resolution and New Normal
beats.purpose: Show the changed world in a concrete image that answers the opening question without explaining it.

hero-journey.label: Hero's Journey (12 Stages)
hero-journey.notes: Mythic transformation arc; strongest when stages are mapped to concrete causal events, not labels.

beats.name: Ordinary World
beats.purpose: Establish the limitation the protagonist has accepted as normal.

beats.name: Call to Adventure
beats.purpose: Deliver the invitation or threat that breaks routine.

beats.name: Refusal of the Call
beats.purpose: Name the fear and the loyalty that keep the protagonist in place.

beats.name: Mentor and Threshold
beats.purpose: Equip the protagonist imperfectly, then cross into the unfamiliar.

beats.name: Tests, Allies, Enemies
beats.purpose: Teach the rules of the new world through encounters that cost something small.

beats.name: Approach to the Inmost Cave
beats.purpose: Narrow the story to the central danger and its preparation.

beats.name: Ordeal
beats.purpose: Stage the near-death experience that forces a change in identity or belief.

beats.name: Reward
beats.purpose: Let the protagonist take the prize and misjudge its meaning.

beats.name: The Road Back
beats.purpose: Trigger the chase or obligation that pulls the protagonist home changed.

beats.name: Resurrection
beats.purpose: Test the new self against the old wound in the most public arena.

beats.name: Return with the Elixir
beats.purpose: Deliver the concrete gift, knowledge, or cost the journey produced.

beats.name: New Normal
beats.purpose: Render the settled aftermath through one ordinary detail that now reads differently.

save-the-cat.label: Save the Cat (15 Beats)
save-the-cat.notes: Dense commercial pacing; every beat is a promise or a payment.

beats.name: Opening Image
beats.purpose: Capture the world and the protagonist's lack in one visual snapshot.

beats.name: Theme Stated
beats.purpose: Have someone state the thematic question the protagonist cannot yet hear.

beats.name: Setup
beats.purpose: Populate the six things that need fixing and the relationships at stake.

beats.name: Catalyst
beats.purpose: Break the world with the inciting event.

beats.name: Debate
beats.purpose: Argue the cost of change in scene, not in summary.

beats.name: Break into Two
beats.purpose: Choose the new world and its rules.

beats.name: B Story
beats.purpose: Introduce the relationship that carries the theme and the protagonist's need.

beats.name: Fun and Games
beats.purpose: Deliver the promise of the premise with escalation and delight.

beats.name: Midpoint
beats.purpose: False victory or false defeat; raise the stakes and change the goal.

beats.name: Bad Guys Close In
beats.purpose: Tighten opposition pressure and erode the protagonist's allies.

beats.name: All Is Lost
beats.purpose: Remove the last support and let the protagonist name their failure.

beats.name: Dark Night of the Soul
beats.purpose: Hold the silence long enough for the lie to surface and break.

beats.name: Break into Three
beats.purpose: A and B stories merge into the idea that makes the finale possible.

beats.name: Finale
beats.purpose: Execute the new plan through the five-point finale and pay the thematic cost.

beats.name: Final Image
beats.purpose: Mirror the opening image to prove the change without stating it.

kishotenketsu.label: Kishotenketsu (4 Movements)
kishotenketsu.notes: Conflict-light structure built on juxtaposition and recontextualization rather than confrontation.

beats.name: Ki - Introduction
beats.purpose: Establish a concrete situation, texture, and relationship without urgency.

beats.name: Sho - Development
beats.purpose: Deepen the situation; let detail accumulate and expectations form.

beats.name: Ten - Twist
beats.purpose: Introduce a structurally unrelated element or perspective that re-reads everything before it.

beats.name: Ketsu - Reconciliation
beats.purpose: Let the two halves resonate into a new, earned meaning without explaining it.

seven-point.label: Seven-Point Story
seven-point.notes: Built backward from the resolution; strong for character-driven genre work.

beats.name: Hook
beats.purpose: Show the protagonist in a state opposite to the ending state.

beats.name: Plot Turn 1
beats.purpose: Introduce the call and the conflict that starts the change.

beats.name: Pinch 1
beats.purpose: Apply pressure that forces the protagonist to act rather than react.

beats.name: Midpoint
beats.purpose: Move the protagonist from reaction to action with a new skill or truth.

beats.name: Pinch 2
beats.purpose: Apply the hardest pressure: the mentor falls, the ally is lost, the plan fails.

beats.name: Plot Turn 2
beats.purpose: Deliver the last piece of information the protagonist needs to win.

beats.name: Resolution
beats.purpose: Show the state opposite to the hook, measured in concrete action.

short-story.label: Short Story (5 Movements)
short-story.notes: Single effect, single turn; every element serves one inevitable outcome.

beats.name: Setup and Pressure
beats.purpose: Locate the character in a specific, unstable situation with a deadline already ticking.

beats.name: Escalation
beats.purpose: Raise the cost of the wrong choice through two or three concrete attempts.

beats.name: Pivot
beats.purpose: Turn the story: reveal, reversal, or refusal that changes the terms.

beats.name: Crisis and Choice
beats.purpose: Force an irreversible choice with no clean option.

beats.name: Resolution and Resonance
beats.purpose: Land the consequence in an image that closes the pattern opened in the first paragraph.

flash.label: Flash / Miniature (3 Movements)
flash.notes: One turn, one image, no runway. Every sentence must carry the ending.

beats.name: Situation
beats.purpose: Anchor time, place, and one pressing physical detail inside the first two sentences.

beats.name: Turn
beats.purpose: Pivot the meaning of everything established so far in a single move.

beats.name: Resonance
beats.purpose: Close on the image that fuses the two meanings and stops.

tv-pilot.label: TV Pilot (5 Beats + Cold Open)
tv-pilot.notes: Engine-first structure: the pilot must prove it can generate episodes, not just tell a story.

beats.name: Cold Open
beats.purpose: Drop the audience into a self-contained jolt that sets voice and world.

beats.name: Premise Ignition
beats.purpose: Introduce the protagonist and the world within the first eight minutes.

beats.name: World and Ensemble Tour
beats.purpose: Meet the ensemble and the institution that will generate weekly conflict.

beats.name: First Act Turn
beats.purpose: Commit the protagonist to the series engine; the door closes.

beats.name: Engine Reveal
beats.purpose: Prove the repeating conflict and the stakes that recur each episode.

beats.name: Pilot Cliffhanger
beats.purpose: End on a question that promises the series without cheating the episode.

comic-22page.label: Comic / Manga Issue (22 Pages)
comic-22page.notes: Page-turn driven; every page ends on a hook and act breaks land on right-hand pages.

beats.name: Establishing Sequence
beats.purpose: Open with a strong visual and the protagonist's ordinary world in three pages.

beats.name: Inciting Turn
beats.purpose: Break the world by page five; end the page on the threat.

beats.name: Response and Rules
beats.purpose: Show how the protagonist responds and what the new rules cost.

beats.name: Midpoint Reversal
beats.purpose: Reverse advantage at the page-eleven spread; change the objective.

beats.name: Escalation Montage
beats.purpose: Compress time with panels that each advance stakes.

beats.name: Setback and Dark Turn
beats.purpose: Strip support and end the page on the lowest image.

beats.name: Climax Spread
beats.purpose: Stage the decisive confrontation across the center spread and a splash page.

beats.name: Resolution and Next Hook
beats.purpose: Close the issue cleanly, then plant the next hook in the final panel.

vn-route.label: Visual Novel Route (6 Nodes)
vn-route.notes: Route-locked structure with explicit flag consequences and per-route payoff.

beats.name: Common Route
beats.purpose: Establish cast, world rules, and the emotional promise shared by every route.

beats.name: First Meaningful Choice
beats.purpose: Offer a choice whose consequence is legible only in hindsight.

beats.name: Route Lock
beats.purpose: Commit the player to one relationship or investigation line.

beats.name: Midpoint Reversal
beats.purpose: Reveal information that reframes the route's central relationship.

beats.name: Trust Collapse
beats.purpose: Test accumulated flags with a high-cost decision.

beats.name: Route Ending
beats.purpose: Pay off the route's promise; end on the emotional image the route earned.

ttrpg-session.label: TTRPG Session (6 Beats)
ttrpg-session.notes: Situation-based prep: prepare pressure, not plot; every beat must survive player divergence.

beats.name: Opening Situation
beats.purpose: Present an immediate problem with a visible clock and a clear stake.

beats.name: Exploration Loop
beats.purpose: Let players choose information channels; each returns a clue and a cost.

beats.name: Complication
beats.purpose: Advance the clock or a faction plan when the players hesitate.

beats.name: Encounter or Negotiation
beats.purpose: Force a contest that can be won, lost, or reframed.

beats.name: Revelation
beats.purpose: Deliver the truth that recontextualizes the situation.

beats.name: Session Close
beats.purpose: Resolve one thread and open two; end with a decision deferred to next session.

children.label: Children (5-8)
children.reading_level: Grades 1-3; short sentences, concrete vocabulary, immediate stakes.
children.content: No on-page violence, death handled gently, endings must be safe and hopeful.
children.pov_limit: Third person limited or first person, single POV.
children.length_note: Chapters 500-1,500 words; picture book text under 1,000 words.

middle-grade.label: Middle Grade (8-12)
middle-grade.reading_level: Grades 4-6; varied sentences, explain unfamiliar terms in context.
middle-grade.content: Peril allowed, graphic violence and sexual content excluded; adult absence creates agency.
middle-grade.pov_limit: One close POV; interiority over dialogue density.

ya.label: Young Adult (12-18)
ya.content: Violence can be present but not gratuitous; romance may be intense without explicit sex.
ya.pov_limit: First person present or close third; one or two POVs.
ya.length_note: 55,000-90,000 words typical; genre may run longer.

adult.label: Adult
adult.content: Defined by the brief's own content limits, not by default.
adult.pov_limit: Any, as long as the structural reason is explicit.

general.label: General / All Ages
general.content: Broad safety envelope: no explicit sex, restrained violence, clear moral stakes.
general.length_note: Flexible; keep scene count proportionate to length.
